feedback.problem:
Rewrite the following expression as the sum of a perfect square and a constant.

$({u}^{2}-3u+\frac{9}{4})+5=(u\,\,-$
{{field-1}} $)^{2}+$
{{field-2}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{u}^{2}-2au+{a}^{2}=(u-a)^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-3u+\frac{9}{4} & = \\ {u}^{2}-3u+{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} & = \\ {u}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{3}{2}u+{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} & = \\ {(u-\frac{3}{2})}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({u}^{2}-3u+\frac{9}{4})+5 & = \\ {(u-\frac{3}{2})}^{2}+5 & .\end{aligned}
$$
